gamenight

gamenight helps you choose a game for your game night. Tell it how many people are playing, how much time you have and the age of the youngest player, and it finds well-rated games that fit, and shows how much better your options get if you allow more time.

Documentation website:https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-noormoolji17/

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

Launch the app 

gamenight::run_app()

The app is for someone hosting a game night, and answers the question: for my group’s size and ages, how much time do we need to allow to play a really well-rated game?

Find games from the console

find_games() returns the games that suit your group, best rated first:

library(gamenight)

find_games(players = 2, max_minutes = 30, youngest_age = 8) |>
  head(5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 12
##       id name           year min_players max_players playing_time min_age rating
##    <int> <chr>         <int>       <int>       <int>        <int>   <int>  <dbl>
## 1    521 Crokinole      1876           2           4           30       8   7.67
## 2 163412 Patchwork      2014           2           2           30       8   7.54
## 3 244522 That's Prett…  2018           1           4           30       8   7.41
## 4 194655 Santorini      2016           2           4           20       8   7.30
## 5 192291 Sushi Go Par…  2016           2           8           20       8   7.28
## # ℹ 4 more variables: average_rating <dbl>, users_rated <int>,
## #   cooperative <lgl>, url <chr>

The data

The package includes games: 20,309 tabletop games (board, card, dice and party games) with their player counts, playing times, suggested minimum ages and ratings. The data comes from BoardGameGeek, via the Kaggle BoardGameGeek Reviews dataset by Jesse van Elteren, as prepared for TidyTuesday on 25 January 2022. The script that downloads and cleans it is in data-raw/games.R. See ?games for what each column means and how the data was cleaned.
